🖍️ Highlighter, step 1: tap the line that shows how all the knights react.
The Lady of Shalott
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1842) · Part IV, the last stanza
Tennyson spells his name Lancelot. Our book says Launcelot.
Who is this? and what is here? And in the lighted palace near Died the sound of royal cheer; And they cross’d themselves for fear, All the knights at Camelot: But Lancelot mused a little space; He said, “She has a lovely face; God in his mercy lend her grace, The Lady of Shalott”.
mused: thought quietly · a little space: a short while · cross’d themselves: made the sign of the cross · lend her grace: give her God’s blessing · royal cheer: the king’s feasting
The line that turns the stanza starts with But. Is that a varied opening?
🎙️ Your turn

Read the whole poem aloud, start to finish. Let the narrator’s calm turn into Launcelot’s quiet last words.

    🍎 At the Board with Professor Lovelore
    Three places your sentences go flat
    Professor Lovelore At the board
    0:38
    An AI-generated character and voice.
    One: the same opening, again and again
    Gareth serves. Gareth waits. Gareth rides out.→Gareth serves and waits. In time, he rides out.
    Two: the and-and chain
    Gawain hides the lace and he goes to the chapel and he is ashamed.→Gawain hides the lace, but at the chapel he is ashamed.
    Three: the tense slip
    Gareth served in the kitchen, and he keeps his promise.→Gareth serves in the kitchen, and he keeps his promise.

    Three lenses for your paragraph

    Before You Submit
    My Evidence Thinking answers in Lessons 1 and 2 are complete sentences. Each names an accurate, specific moment and its chapter.
    The Knight’s Gallery is finished: all 20 plaques judged, two knights chosen, three plaques each in book order with a phrase, my claim written, and all five outline lines present. The Round Table has six seats in order, and the other side names a real moment and passes the fairness check.
    The Lists: my run sheet is filled, I checked “I said my whole argument aloud,” and I wrote one sentence on the hardest part to say.
    My Quick Write is 150 to 200 words. It states the strongest case for the other knight fairly with a real moment, then answers it with a real moment from my knight. It has no straw man and no either/or.
    I combined at least one pair of sentences and varied at least one opening. My verbs are in the present tense, my quotation punctuation is correct, and my before-and-after shows a change.
    My introduction has a hook, a purpose, a claim naming both knights, and background. My conclusion says what the comparison reveals. I saved Draft2 with the right file name and I will upload it as the second file.
